headline: Notting Hill Carnival marks 60 years, with 243 arrests on its opening day
dek: The Metropolitan Police revised Sunday's arrest count up from 169 to 243 as the day ended, and said 61 of those arrests followed live facial recognition matches. The main parade ran on Monday.
summary: Europe's largest street festival marked its 60th year in west London this weekend, with the Metropolitan Police reporting 243 arrests on Sunday and organisers arguing the event is judged unfairly on crime.

image.alt: A close-up of steel pan drums set up on a city street.

body.text: The Notting Hill Carnival held its main parade through west London on Monday, closing a weekend that marked the festival's 60th year. ITV News London and BBC News both reported that around two million people were expected across the bank holiday weekend, an estimate rather than a counted figure — no authority publishes a verified attendance for the event.

The carnival was first held in 1966, growing out of London's Caribbean community and the cultural life of the Windrush generation. It now runs over three days: a national steelband competition on the Saturday, a family day on the Sunday, and the adult parade on the Monday.

The Metropolitan Police said 243 people were arrested during Sunday, the first full day of the policing operation. Of those, 97 arrests were made on approaches to the event and the remainder inside the carnival area, for offences including drug possession, weapon possession, assault and sexual offences. The force said 61 of the arrests followed identifications by live facial recognition.

That total is a revision upward during the day. In an update issued on Sunday evening, the Met gave a running figure of 169 arrests as of 19:45 — 142 inside the event perimeter and 27 on the approaches, with 29 attributed to live facial recognition. Both counts are provisional, and the force has not yet published a figure covering Monday or the weekend as a whole.

More than 7,000 officers were deployed across west London, alongside over 3,000 stewards, roughly double the usual number, according to the Met. The force said it had used bail conditions to ban more than 330 people from attending. BBC News reported, citing the Met, that two people were treated for non-life-threatening wounds after knife attacks on Sunday.

The figures are not straightforwardly comparable with earlier years. The Met's own release after the 2024 carnival recorded 102 arrests on the Sunday and 349 across the weekend, at a time when live facial recognition was not being used at the same scale. A change in tactics can move an arrest count without telling you much about how the day itself went.
Matthew Phillip, chief executive of the carnival, told BBC News it was unfair that the event is always identified as a cause of violence, and put the relationship the other way round.
It is a victim of crime rather than a perpetrator.
body.cite: Matthew Phillip, chief executive of Notting Hill Carnival, via BBC News

body.text: The carnival route passes close to Grenfell Tower, and the weekend again included a 72-second silence for the 72 people killed in the June 2017 fire.

Ahead of this year's event, the Greater London Authority announced additional funding of £4.66 million, on top of £946,300 City Hall had already committed, aimed at safety improvements after an independent review raised concerns about crowding. Organisers also ran a £60,000 community support fund to help participants take part, ITV News London reported.
Notting Hill Carnival is one of our capital's biggest events, drawing Londoners and visitors from across the globe to West London every year in a fantastic celebration of Caribbean culture.
body.cite: Sadiq Khan, Mayor of London, via the Greater London Authority

body.text: The GLA announcement also cited an economic figure that is often quoted for the carnival — a direct or net economic impact of more than £396 million a year. That estimate comes from 2024 research commissioned by The Voice newspaper and carried out by the JN Bank economist James Williams, not from an official statistical body, and should be read as one commissioned study rather than a settled number.

uncertain: The Metropolitan Police's arrest figures for Sunday are provisional and were revised upward during the day, from 169 at 19:45 to 243 for the full day.

It has not been stated whether the two people treated for wounds on Sunday were hurt in the same incident, and no charges arising from it have been reported.
